newsitem.title: BRAZIL: BRAZIL CELL BID SEEN BEDEVILED BY LEGAL CHALLENGE.
newsitem.headline: BRAZIL CELL BID SEEN BEDEVILED BY LEGAL CHALLENGE.

text.p: Friday's awarding of a cellular phone concession covering Sao Paulo state to a Brazilian-Swedish group was welcomed by analysts, but they warned it may be overturned by a court ruling next week.
Bank analysts said the Supreme Tribunal of Justice (STJ) may still disqualify the Tess group, which had obtained an injunction to allow it to take part in the bidding for B Band cellular area No. 2.
"Can it be overturned? I'd say the odds are 50-50," said Marcelo Mollica of local investment bank Banco Icatu.
"There are good arguments on both sides."

Tess, which includes Sweden's state-owned telecom Telia, was among five groups the Brazilian government ruled ineligible to participate in B Band privatization auctions. But it appealed the decision and sought an injunction to stay in the running.

On Friday, Tess beat four other groups for the license to operate cellphone services in Sao Paulo state with an offer of 1.326 billion reais ($1.22 billion) -- a 121 percent premium over the base price. Analysts said the price for the concession was hefty but within market projections of premiums ranging from 70 percent to 200 percent.

However, the STJ is expected to rule next week on the initial disqualification. The Communications Ministry said Tess violated bidding rules by failing to use an official Brazilian translator for tender documents and did not have a legal representative here. "Now, it all depends on the lawyers and on the legal debate," said Sergio Missima of Fator Securities.

If Tess were disqualified, the area No. 2 license could go to the second-place Avantel group, made up of Brazil's Odebrecht ODE_p.SA, Camargo Correa and Unibanco and U.S.-based AirTouch Communications Inc, which bid 1.224 billion reais.
As part of its bid, Tess offered an initial cellular fee of 200 reais, a monthly subscription charge of 23 reais and a basket of tariffs totalling 69.80 reais.
Analysts said those rates are lower than those charged by Telesp, a unit of Brazilian federal telecom giant Telebras serving Sao Paulo state, but they do not threaten to severely undercut them.
On the other hand, Avantel's proposed tariff basket of 48.80 reais and monthly subscription charge of 4.60 reais would cause Telesp's rates to tumble, they said.
While that would be good for consumers, Avantel's tariffs would hurt Telesp and Telebras revenues, stock prices and privatization prices, analysts said.
"If Avantel turns out to be the winner, that would be terrible for the market. Their rates are so low," said an analyst at a foreign investment bank here.
"From the market's point of view, it would be preferable if Tess stayed the winner," Icatu's Mollica said.
Further complicating matters was the uncertainty surrounding another legal challenge to the area No. 2 tender.
Tess' winning bid may be ambushed by an unopened bid by the Telet group, which has appealed its disqualification in July by Communications Minister Sergio Motta.
On Friday, a court ruled the ministry must keep the bid by consortium, which includes BCE Inc's Bell Canada and Telesystem International Wireless Inc, until the case has been decided.
However, a local news agency reported Friday after area No. 2 tender envelopes were opened that Telet was considering dropping its bid.
One analyst said that dropping the bid would imply its offer was lower than Tess', while continuing the legal battle would mean the group had bid more and sees a chance to win the concession.
((--Sao Paulo newsroom 5511 248 5413))
